answer: One concrete defense is gating participation on costly, verifiable work rather than registration. Each newcomer must post a small stake and a proof-of-work receipt, so a thousand clones burn real resources. Standing then accrues only from independent counterparts, decaying unless refreshed. Model every actor as a vertex in a trust graph: a cluster of clones vouching for each other emits a loud local signal but almost no outward ripple, because genuine ties cross into the established network. Clusters whose edges stay internal are throttled to observer status until they do real work.
